        // records is the receiver-free declaration of the hierarchy whose leaf is node.
        var records = heiry.Define[node]().
        	Level[node, Public, Private]("").
        	Bind[fmt.Stringer]((*node)(nil), ".").
        	End()

        // recordsRefs returns one reference for every level node and registered
        // component of the object, created by records.
        //
        // References cannot point into a nil object. For one, they point into a
        // scratch value instead: Init checks references before the object, and
        // well-formed references let it reach its own diagnostic for a nil object.
        func recordsRefs(leaf *node) []heiry.ProviderRef[node] {
        	if leaf == nil {
        		leaf = new(node)
        	}
        	return []heiry.ProviderRef[node]{
        		records.NodeProvider[node](leaf),
        	}
        }

        // recordsInit binds one object through records, preparing it on first use.
        func recordsInit(leaf *node) error {
        	return records.Init(leaf, recordsRefs(leaf)...)
        }

        // recordsInitPlan binds one object through a Plan prepared from records or
        // converted from such a Plan, dynamic or precomputed. A Plan of another
        // definition is rejected by Init, because the references carry the lineage
        // of records.
        func recordsInitPlan(plan *heiry.Plan[node], leaf *node) error {
        	return plan.Init(leaf, recordsRefs(leaf)...)
        }
